# Maintain the compliance obligations calendar

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

At formation and when locations, headcount, financing, products or legal requirements change. An owned obligations register with source-backed due dates, evidence locations and escalation rules.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Inventory the facts that drive obligations

agent-runnable


Compile entity types, jurisdictions, registrations, workforce locations, contractual commitments and reporting periods. Link each fact to its private source and flag outdated or missing information.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Confirm obligations and dates with the responsible advisers

human · human approval required


Ask finance, employment, privacy and company-law advisers to identify applicable filings, renewals and reviews. Record the exact authority or agreement and how the date is calculated; unresolved applicability remains an open item.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Create the owned calendar and evidence register

agent-runnable


Record each obligation, accountable owner, preparation lead time, reviewer and completion evidence. Separate statutory, contractual and internal deadlines so a preferred internal date does not become a claimed legal deadline.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve reminders and escalation coverage

human · human approval required


Assign backups for absent owners, specify escalation when evidence is missing and confirm who authorizes filings or payments. Test a representative reminder without submitting an external filing.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile completed obligations and refresh the calendar

agent-runnable


Compare calendar items with receipts and review changes in the business before the next period. Carry unresolved or rejected work forward visibly rather than marking an obligation complete because a reminder was dismissed.

- Verify: An owned obligations register with source-backed due dates, evidence locations and escalation rules.
- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)
